newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end weaker, up from earlier lows.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end weaker, up from earlier lows.

text.p: Toronto's key stock index ended lower on Tuesday despite recouping some earlier losses after a late-session bounce on Wall Street.
The TSE 300 Composite Index fell 19.77 points to close at 5821.01 in brisk turnover of 80.4 million shares worth C$1.3 billion ($936 million).
Declining issues outpaced advances 557 to 369, with 282 issues holding steady.

"Toward the end of the day the rockets seemed to fire and New York took off and closed up 53 points, Toronto followed suit but had less of a thrust," said Ira Katzin, investment advisor at RBC Dominion Securities.
"So the loss is less at the end of the day than it had been during the day," he added.
Eleven of Toronto's 14 sub-indexes lost ground in the session, led by metals and oils.
Metals and minerals shed 47.19 points or 0.92 percent to 5069.99, while the energy group fell 50.64 points or 0.81 percent to 6165.69.
Conglomerates, pipelines and real estate ended the day higher.
Bre-X Minerals Ltd was the most active stock, ending down C23 cents at C$2.29 as more than 13.7 million shares traded hands.
Katzin said Bre-X will hold the market's interest for a while to come.
"Bre-X of course, again, continues to lead the markets day in and day out. The volatility in the stock, in order to watch it you have to have strong stomachs and a temperament of iron," said Katzin.
Shares in the troubled Calgary exploration company lost C66 cents on Monday.

Alcan Aluminium Ltd. ended C50 cents lower at C$44.40 in healthy trade ahead of a potentially disappointing first-quarter earnings report expected later in the week. Shares in the Montreal-based company were off C90 cents earlier in the session.

Shares in funeral chain Loewen Group Inc extended a recent slide as investors anticipated a stock offering from the company in coming months. Loewen ended down C85 cents at C$40.15 in Toronto and 1/2 at $29.00 in New York.
